info.name: Document Insights API
info.description:
Tests for the Document Insights API: submit document text, a worker summarizes it in the
background (mocked, 10–30 s, ~10% failure rate), clients poll for the result.
Polling `GET /documents/{id}` returns only `document_id` and `status` while the document is
`queued` or `processing`, and the whole document once it's `completed` or `failed`.

**Start the app first:** `docker compose up --build` from the repo root, then check
`GET {{baseUrl}}/health`.

**Run everything:** open the Collection Runner (or `postman collection run`) with the
*Document Insights API - Local* environment. A full run takes ~15–100 s, mostly waiting on the worker.

**Variables**

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `http://localhost:8000` | change if you set `API_PORT` |
| `userId` | `alice` | user for the lifecycle folder |
| `otherUserId` | `bob` | second user, who gets the same content from the cache |
| `maxActiveJobs` | `3` | must match `MAX_ACTIVE_JOBS_PER_USER` |
| `pollIntervalMs` | `3000` | delay between polls |
| `maxPolls` | `60` | give up polling after this many tries |

Other variables (`documentId`, `docContent`, ...) are set by scripts during a run.

item.name: 1. Health
item.description: Liveness/readiness. `200` with `ok` (or `degraded` when Redis is down), `503` when MongoDB is down.

exec: pm.test('Overall status is ok or degraded', () => {
pm.test('Status is degraded exactly when Redis is down', () => {

request.description:
Checks MongoDB and Redis.

- `200` `{"status": "ok"}`: everything is up
- `200` `{"status": "degraded"}`: Redis is down; the API still works and falls back to MongoDB
- `503` `{"status": "unavailable"}`: MongoDB is down
A well-formed `X-Request-ID` (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}`) is kept and returned, so a request can be traced across services and in the logs.

request.description: An `X-Request-ID` that doesn't match `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}` is discarded and the server generates its own (32 hex chars).

item.name: 2. Document lifecycle
item.description:
The main flow: submit a document, poll it until the worker finishes, submit the same content again
(returns the same document), send it as another user (served from the summary cache), then list
the user's documents.

Run this folder in order (Collection Runner or `postman collection run`). Requests pass ids
to each other through collection variables (`documentId`, `docContent`, ...).

Processing is mocked: 10–30 s per attempt, ~10% of attempts fail, up to 3 attempts with backoff.
**Poll until finished** loops on itself (every `pollIntervalMs`, at most `maxPolls` times) when run
in the Runner/CLI. Sent by hand, it just shows the current status; click Send again to re-poll.

exec: // Unique content per run, so this is never a cache hit and always queues a real job.
'Revenue grew 12% in Q3. Costs stayed flat. Headcount rose by 4. Run ' + runId + '.');
pm.test('New content is queued: only document_id and status', () => {
pm.test('Location header points at the new document', () => {

request.description:
Submits a document for summarization. Returns `201` with the new `document_id` and a
`Location: /documents/{id}` header.

- `{document_id, status: queued}` for new content: poll `GET /documents/{id}` for the result.
- The whole document, `status: completed` with `summary` set, when identical content was
  summarized before (cache hit).
- `200` with the user's existing document when they already sent this content, unless it `failed`.

The pre-request script makes the content unique per run so this always starts a real job.
`422` on invalid input, `429` when the user already has `MAX_ACTIVE_JOBS_PER_USER` jobs in flight.

- While it's `queued` or `processing`: only `document_id` and `status`.
- Once it's `completed` or `failed`: the whole document, including `content`, with `summary`

request.description:
Same endpoint as **Get document**, but in the Runner/CLI it re-runs itself every `pollIntervalMs`

Sending content this user already sent returns their existing document instead of creating another:
`200` with the same `document_id` and `Location`, in the same shape as **Get document** (the whole

A `failed` document doesn't block a fresh try, so resubmitting it creates a new one (`201`).
Tests are skipped in that case.

item.name: 4. Rate limit
item.description:
Each user can have at most `MAX_ACTIVE_JOBS_PER_USER` (default 3) documents `queued` or `processing`.
The next submission gets `429` until one finishes.

Uses a fresh throwaway user per run (`rlUserId`) so it doesn't interfere with `userId`. Set the
`maxActiveJobs` variable if you changed `MAX_ACTIVE_JOBS_PER_USER`.

Side effect: leaves `maxActiveJobs` real jobs in the queue; the worker finishes them within a minute or so.

exec: // First submission of the scenario: pick a fresh user.

request.description:
Submits `maxActiveJobs` documents (each with unique content, so none are cache hits).
In the Runner/CLI it repeats itself until the limit is reached; sent by hand, click Send
`maxActiveJobs` times.

exec: pm.test('Status is 429 Too Many Requests', () => pm.response.to.have.status(429));
pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include(`You already have ${limit} documents queued or processing`);
// Reset so the next run starts with a fresh user.

request.description: One more than the limit: `429 Too Many Requests`.
